transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-20
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramirez (Aurelia VP Eng), Tom Chen (Aurelia ML Infra), Priya Kapoor (Aurelia Security), Alex Wu (Aurelia SRE)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on latency and throughput requirements for an in-product recommendation/chat assistant; explored Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options and discussed p95 targets, concurrency, streaming behavior, and benchmark approach. Agreed to run a Dedicated trial benchmark and exchange security docs.

Topics:
- p95 latency SLOs (50ms-400ms range)
- concurrency and tokens/sec targets (200-800 concurrent users, 5k-20k tokens/sec aggregate)
- quality vs cost trade-offs: batching, quantization, KV cache
- streaming latencies and partial token delivery
- security: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, RBAC, encryption/KMS, data residency

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena, AE on the Redwood team, and with me is Marcus, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Sofia Ramirez: Good, thanks. Sofia here. We wanted to dig into latency and throughput details - p95 in particular. We run recommendations and a chat experience in our web and mobile apps so tail latency matters.
[00:18] Marcus Li: Great; can you give us the ballpark p95 target and concurrency? Also useful to know streaming vs non-streaming, and whether you need partial token delivery for UI.
[00:27] Tom Chen: We're aiming for p95 generation latency under 250ms for short prompts (~64 tokens) and under 600ms for longer flows (~512 tokens). Concurrency expected to ramp: 200 steady users, peak 600-800 concurrent generating requests during promos. We measure per-request p95 at our edge.
[00:48] Alex Wu: Also want streaming for chat so tokens start appearing quickly - front-end uses partial streaming to render typing indicator. If streaming is slow, UX suffers.
[00:56] Marcus Li: Makes sense. For Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: Hosted is easiest to get started but shared capacity may have variable tail behavior; Dedicated gives predictable p95 because you reserve GPU pools and throughput. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives full isolation and lower network hop variance if you colocate, but adds operational overhead.
[01:15] Sofia Ramirez: Right. We're evaluating tradeoffs. Latency consistency is most important, cost after that. We also have strict data residency and encryption needs - Priya, can you add?
[01:24] Priya Kapoor: Yes, from security side we need SOC 2 compliance, KMS for keys, audit logs, SSO/SAML and RBAC. Also network constraints: ideally VPC peering or private link for Dedicated, and for Private deployment we need an architecture review.
[01:38] Lena Park: Redwood supports SOC2, SAML SSO, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs. For Dedicated we can set up VPC peering and private endpoints. We'll send the security whitepaper after the call.
[01:50] Tom Chen: For benchmarking, we want to validate tokens/sec and per-token latency. Do you have a lab benchmark template we can run? We prefer to run both streaming and non-streaming tests and measure end-to-end p95 including network.
[02:03] Marcus Li: Yes, we'll share a benchmark template. Typical metrics we capture: p50/p90/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory, KV cache hit rate, and how batching affects tail. For streaming, we measure time-to-first-token and tokens-per-second delivered to the client.
[02:22] Sofia Ramirez: One question - how does batching impact p95 for short prompts? We worry batching to improve throughput increases latency for interactive flows.
[02:31] Marcus Li: Good question. Batching increases throughput but can add queuing latency. Redwood's runtime supports dynamic batching with latency SLOs where we cap maximum batch delay; you can enforce strict latency windows for interactive routes and larger batching for background bulk jobs. Also prefix/KV cache helps reduce work per request which improves tail.
[02:50] Alex Wu: Do you support per-route configs? We want chat to be low-latency and some recommendation jobs can be batched.
[02:55] Lena Park: Yes, per-route and model-specific profiles, and you can pin models or fall back to cheaper variants under load.
[03:03] Tom Chen: About numbers - our internal load tests show we need ~10k tokens/sec sustained during peak; peak bursts can be up to 20k tokens/sec for short periods. If we target 500 concurrent streams, what's realistic p95 on Dedicated?
[03:17] Marcus Li: Depends on model size and hardware. As an example, on an A100-like Dedicated pool with optimized kernels we see ~1200-1500 tokens/sec per GPU for xT smaller models (quantized), and lower for larger models. For 500 concurrent interactive streams at 64-token responses, throughput vs latency depends on batching and KV cache. With Dedicated and streaming enabled we can often meet sub-250ms p95 for short prompts if you provision enough GPU capacity and use caching/quantization. We'll need to run a representative workload to be sure.
[03:48] Priya Kapoor: We also need to confirm data retention - do you keep logs of prompts by default? And can we disable retention?
[03:56] Lena Park: By default Hosted is ephemeral for customer prompt content but we have retention policies; Dedicated and Private offer stricter retention controls and the ability to opt out of storing prompts. We'll include details in the security docs.
[04:07] Sofia Ramirez: Great. For benchmarking, we'd like Redwood to run a baseline on Hosted and then a Dedicated trial with our prompts. Can you provision Dedicated trial capacity?
[04:15] Marcus Li: Yes, we can spin up a short Dedicated trial pool. We'll propose a test plan: 1) baseline on Hosted with synthetic traffic; 2) Dedicated trial with your prompt set and network topology (we recommend running from your edge or via VPC peering to measure real network RTT); 3) streaming vs non-streaming runs, varying concurrency (200, 400, 600) and measuring p95/end-to-end.
[04:39] Tom Chen: For the Dedicated trial, can you expose GPU metrics and per-token cost breakdown? Our finance team wants to estimate cost per 1k tokens.
[04:49] Lena Park: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and per model. We'll include cost projection in the follow-up.
[04:58] Alex Wu: One gotcha: our clients are global; we care about region routing and fallbacks. How does Redwood handle multi-region routing for latency-critical traffic?
[05:06] Marcus Li: We support region routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants in other regions. For the lowest latency you can provision Dedicated capacity in target regions. We also have smart routing by latency and cost.
[05:18] Sofia Ramirez: Any limitations on streaming? Are partial tokens flushed early or chunked regularly? We need consistent small packets for our front-end.
[05:26] Marcus Li: Streaming is configurable; we can tune chunk sizes and timeouts. Time-to-first-token is typically dominated by model compute and network; for short outputs we can prioritize fast first token by disabling large batch delays for chat route.
[05:39] Priya Kapoor: Regarding encryption: if we use customer-managed KMS, does Redwood ever hold plaintext keys or decrypted data?
[05:46] Lena Park: No, with customer-managed KMS we keep encrypted at rest and keys are only accessible via your KMS. We'll provide architecture notes.
[05:54] Tom Chen: For the benchmark, what sample prompts should we send? We have a mix: 40% short recommendation prompts (~20-60 tokens), 50% conversational chat (~40-200 tokens), 10% long summarization (~512+ tokens).
[06:07] Marcus Li: That's helpful. We'll template the tests to reflect that distribution. Also capture cache warm-up behavior since KV cache improves downstream token perf.
[06:18] Sofia Ramirez: OK, timeline - if Marcus can provision Dedicated trial and run initial benchmarks by next week, we can review results and then decide on pilot.
[06:26] Lena Park: Sounds good. We'll send over the benchmark template and security docs today. Marcus will kick off the Dedicated trial.
[06:33] Priya Kapoor: Please include SOC2 report and network topology examples; we'll need those for procurement.
[06:38] Lena Park: Will do.
[06:42] Sofia Ramirez: Anything else from your side?
[06:46] Alex Wu: One last thing - any known differences in p95 behavior between quantized vs fp16 models? We've seen quantization reduce throughput variability but sometimes increases single-token latency.
[06:55] Marcus Li: Correct - quantization can reduce memory and increase throughput but depending on kernels it might change per-token latency slightly. We'll surface recommended quant profiles per model for your workload in the benchmark results.
[07:06] Lena Park: Ok I'll do a quick recap of action items...
[07:09] Lena Park (recap): 1) Marcus to provision Dedicated trial and run tokens/sec + p95 benchmarks with your prompt set; 2) Sofia to send prompt set and p95 SLOs; 3) Priya to confirm KMS/compliance needs; 4) Redwood to send security docs and benchmark template.
[07:26] Sofia Ramirez: Thanks all, that's perfect. Looking forward to the trial.
[07:30] Lena Park: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and create the tech-deep-dive invite.

End of transcript.
